findings.title: Second `self.downsize` definition silently overwrites the 4-argument one
findings.body: `self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` (line 145) is immediately redefined by `self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` (line 149). In Ruby the later definition wins, so the 4-arg form is dead code and every existing caller that passes width and height separately (e.g. `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, w, h)`) now either raises `ArgumentError` (5 args) or passes the height Integer as `opts`, which then blows up with `TypeError: no implicit conversion of Symbol into Integer` inside `downsize_instructions` when evaluating `opts[:force_aspect_ratio]`. If both forms are needed, use a single method that accepts either a dimension string or width/height, and update all call sites.

findings.title: In-place downsize can destroy the uploaded file and the failure result is ignored
findings.body: `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)` uses the same path for input and output, so ImageMagick/gifsicle truncates and rewrites the only copy of the user's upload. `convert_with` swallows errors (`rescue` -> `false`) and this return value is not checked, so a failed or partially written conversion leaves a truncated/empty file that is then handed to `Upload.create_for`, producing a corrupt upload instead of an error. Write to a separate temp file and only swap it in when the conversion reports success; abort the loop as soon as `downsize` returns false.

findings.title: Loop re-reads size from a Tempfile handle whose file was rewritten by an external process
findings.body: The loop condition and the later `Upload.create_for(..., tempfile.size, ...)` read size through the still-open `Tempfile` object after an external binary rewrote `tempfile.path`. If the tool writes a new file and renames it over the path (gifsicle does this, and some ImageMagick delegates do too), the open descriptor still refers to the unlinked original inode, so `tempfile.size` returns the stale (large) size: the loop keeps re-converting for all 5 attempts and the recorded filesize can disagree with the stored bytes. Re-open/stat the path (`File.size(tempfile.path)`) after each conversion instead of trusting the cached handle.

findings.title: Percentage dimension is invalid for the animated-GIF (gifsicle) code path
findings.body: With `SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails` enabled and a `.gif` upload, `optimize` dispatches to `downsize_instructions_animated`, which builds `gifsicle <from> --colors=256 --resize-fit 80% --optimize=3 --output <to>`. `--resize-fit` only accepts pixel geometry (`WxH`, `_xH`, ...), not a percentage, so gifsicle exits with an error; because input and output are the same path the GIF may also be clobbered. Use `--scale 0.8` for gifsicle, or compute explicit pixel dimensions before calling downsize.

findings.title: Client-side size limit hardcoded to 10MB, ignoring max_attachment_size_kb / max_image_size_kb
findings.body: `validateUploadedFile` previously used `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`; it now hardcodes 10240 KB for every type. Non-image attachments are not downsized server-side, so a site configured with a smaller `max_attachment_size_kb` will let users pick files that the server then rejects (and the `file_too_large` alert quotes 10240 KB, a number the admin never configured). Conversely, sites with a larger configured limit now have uploads blocked in the browser. The `type` argument is also no longer used for the size check. Keep using the site setting for attachments, and only bypass it for images that the server will downsize.

findings.title: 413 error message hardcodes 10MB instead of the configured limit
findings.body: In `displayErrorForUpload`, the HTTP 413 branch now reports `10 * 1024` KB regardless of the site's `max_image_size_kb`/`max_attachment_size_kb` or the web server's `client_max_body_size`. Users on sites with a different limit get a misleading maximum size in the alert.

findings.title: API URL download limit hardcoded to 10MB for all upload types
findings.body: `FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...)` replaces the `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`-derived limit. This applies to every `type`, including attachments which are never downsized afterwards, so an API user can make the server fetch and buffer up to 10MB per request even when the administrator configured a much smaller maximum. Derive the cap from the relevant site setting (with an explicit, bounded allowance for images that will be downsized).

findings.title: Up to five full ImageMagick + ImageOptim passes run inline per upload
findings.body: Each loop iteration shells out to `convert` and then `ImageOptim.new.optimize_image!` (inside `convert_with`), so a single large upload can trigger five full re-encodes plus five lossless-optimizer runs while occupying a request/Defer worker. For multi-megabyte images this is seconds to minutes of CPU per upload and is trivially triggerable by any logged-in user. Compute the target scale from the current/desired byte ratio so one or two passes suffice, and skip the ImageOptim pass for intermediate iterations.

findings.title: No tests for the new auto-downsize behaviour or the changed downsize signature
findings.body: The PR adds a size-reduction loop in `create_upload` and changes `OptimizedImage.downsize`/`optimize` signatures, but no specs are added or updated. There is no coverage for: an oversized image being reduced below `max_image_size_kb`, an image still too large after 5 attempts, a non-image skipping the loop, or the new `downsize(from, to, dimensions)` form. Existing specs calling `OptimizedImage.downsize(from, to, w, h)` or `OptimizedImage.dimensions` (now removed) would also fail silently unnoticed without updates.
